title: Dose-response relationship of autonomic nervous system responses to individualized training impulse in marathon runners
authors: Manzi V, Castagna C, Padua E, Lombardo M, D'Ottavio S, Massaro M, Volterrani M, Iellamo F
journal: American Journal of Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology
population: Eight recreational long-distance athletes followed for 6 months of training culminating in a marathon
findings: Individualized load was monitored with a modified TRIMP (TRIMPi) built from each athlete's own HR and lactate profile from a treadmill test; monthly TRIMPi steadily increased over the training period.

All autonomic parameters (HRV spectral measures, baroreflex sensitivity) were significantly related to dose by a second-order regression model (r2 0.90 to 0.99; P < 0.001), bell-shaped or U-shaped with the extreme at the highest TRIMPi.
The LF component of HRV at the last recording session was significantly and inversely correlated with the time needed to complete the marathon.
Authors interpret a progressive shift toward sympathetic predominance and suggest LF at peak load could predict achievement in this population.
limitations: Eight recreational athletes, no control group, needs a laboratory HR-lactate profile. Does not compare TRIMP versions or test the sex-specific Banister constants; the abstract does not state the weighting used. The fitted r2 values describe 6 monthly points per person, so they overstate precision.
implications: Where the user has a lactate-threshold or field-test HR profile, offer an individualized exponential-weighted TRIMP as an optional upgrade over the generic Banister weighting.
Use weekly or monthly TRIMP trend, not a single-session value, as a build/recovery input.
With n = 8, keep any thresholds from this paper out of hard rules; supporting rationale only.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, AJP Heart Circ Physiol, 2009, first author Manzi. Abstract read in Europe PMC; numbers match. This is not a source for the 1.92/1.67 Banister constants, which remain unverified in this corpus (Banister 1991 is a book chapter that is not indexed).
